scale_009:n1.prompt:
You are helping me create services in {{vendor}}, our incident management platform, as part of setting up on-call and incident response. Approval is required before any changes go live, so you must prepare everything and then stop for human sign-off.

Before starting, ask me for: (1) the list of services/teams that need incident coverage (e.g., API, web app, database, payments), (2) the monitoring/alerting tools that will send alerts into each service (e.g., our APM, uptime checker, log alerting), and (3) any naming convention or existing team structure I want reflected in service names and descriptions.

Using your configured credentials, connect to {{vendor}} via its documented public API or official MCP server integration if available. For each service I specify, draft: a clear service name, a description of what it covers and which team owns it, the escalation policy it should link to (ask me if one already exists or needs to be created), and the alert-routing/integration source (which monitoring tool feeds it and any routing conditions based on severity or alert type). Where {{vendor}} supports scoped or least-privilege API credentials for agent access, prepare a recommendation for what scope to request rather than using broad admin access.

Compile all of this into a single checklist or draft configuration document showing, per service: name, description, owner, escalation policy link, and alert source/routing rules. Do not create, modify, or push any services or integrations into {{vendor}} yet.

Report back with the full draft list of proposed services and their configurations, clearly flagged as pending, and stop for human sign-off before any service is actually created in {{vendor}}.

scale_009:n2.prompt:
You are helping me set up on-call rotation schedules in {{vendor}} (our incident-management tool) as part of standing up our on-call & incidents process. Approval is required before any changes go live, so you must prepare everything and then stop for human sign-off — do not activate or publish any schedule yourself.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available via my configured credentials, including: our {{vendor}} account/subdomain, the list of on-call teams/services, each team member's name and time zone, desired rotation type per team (e.g., weekly, daily, round-robin, or follow-the-sun layered rotation), rotation start date/time, and any coverage exceptions (holidays, business-hours-only, etc.).

Then, using {{vendor}}'s API (or its dashboard if the API isn't accessible with current credentials), draft one rotation schedule per team that reflects how that team actually works — including correct time zones, rotation layers if multiple cadences overlap (e.g., a business-hours layer plus a nights/weekends layer), and round-robin ordering of members. Where the API supports it, prefer creating schedules programmatically so the setup is reproducible and documented.

Do not activate, save-as-live, or notify anyone yet. Instead, produce a clear summary for each proposed schedule: team name, rotation type, layers, time zone, member order, and start date. Present this as a checklist I can review.

When finished, report back with: (1) the full list of draft schedules and their configurations, (2) any teams or details you couldn't get info for, and (3) a note confirming these are staged drafts awaiting my explicit approval before being applied. Then stop for human sign-off.

scale_009:n3.prompt:
You are helping me configure escalation policies in {{vendor}} (our incident-management tool) as part of setting up on-call & incidents. I will need to approve these changes before they go live, so your job is to prepare everything and then stop.

First, ask me for anything you don't already have: my {{vendor}} account access (assume you can use your configured credentials), the on-call schedules already created (or ask me to list the teams/services involved), and any existing escalation conventions we follow (e.g., how many minutes before escalating, who the fallback responders are).

Then, using {{vendor}}'s documented API or admin interface, draft one or more escalation policies that:
- Tie to the correct on-call schedule(s) and service(s)
- Define multiple escalation steps (e.g., primary on-call, then secondary, then a manager or fallback responder)
- Set a reasonable delay before escalating an unacknowledged page at each step (ask me to confirm timing if not specified, e.g., 5-10 minutes)
- Include a repeat/looping rule so escalation cycles continue until someone acknowledges

Do not create or activate the policies yet. Instead, produce a clear draft summary for each policy showing: policy name, associated service(s), escalation steps in order, delay per step, and repeat behavior. Present this as a checklist I can review.

Once the draft is ready, stop for human sign-off — do not submit, save, or activate any policy in {{vendor}} without my explicit approval.

Report back with: the full draft policy details, any assumptions you made (e.g., default delay times), and a short list of open questions where you need my input before finalizing.

scale_009:n4.prompt:
You are helping me connect our error-tracking/observability tool ({{vendor}}) to PagerDuty for automated incident alerting, as part of our on-call & incidents setup. Before starting, ask me for: (1) our {{vendor}} account/org details and confirmation you can access it with configured credentials, (2) our PagerDuty account and the service/escalation policy this integration should route into, and (3) which error severities or issue types should page on-call versus just notify a channel.

Once you have these, prepare (but do not apply) the following: a plan to enable the {{vendor}}-to-PagerDuty integration so that grouped application errors (with stack traces, release tracking, and regression detection) generate alerts; a proposed routing/grouping/silencing scheme so only actionable, deduplicated issues page the on-call engineer via the existing escalation policy and schedules; and a webhook configuration draft so {{vendor}} alert events can also notify a webhook endpoint for automated remediation or agent triggers, if we want that. Document exactly which settings would need to change in both {{vendor}} and PagerDuty (alert rules, webhook URLs, severity mappings, escalation policy targets), and produce a clear before/after summary plus a rollback note.

Do not enable, save, or activate any integration, webhook, or alert rule changes yourself — because this step requires a human to explicitly approve before changes are applied, you must stop for human sign-off once the plan and draft configuration are ready. Report back with the full proposed configuration, open questions, and a checklist I can review and approve before you or I apply it.

scale_009:n5.prompt:
You are helping me set up the incident chat channel for our PagerDuty on-call/incident process, using {{vendor}} (our team-chat tool). Approval is required before anything is applied: prepare everything, then stop for human sign-off.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already known: my {{vendor}} workspace/org details, the desired channel name (e.g. 'incidents' or 'sev1-incidents'), whether it should be public or private, and which teams/roles should have membership.

Then, using my configured credentials:
1. Prepare the channel creation using the {{vendor}} CLI equivalent of: buzz channels create --name "<incident-channel-name>" --type stream --visibility open — adjusting the name and visibility per my answers.
2. Draft a short channel description/topic explaining its purpose (live incident coordination, linked to PagerDuty alerts).
3. Identify what integration is needed to connect PagerDuty to this channel — note whether it should use a prebuilt app-directory integration, an incoming webhook, or a bot via the events/gateway API — and prepare the configuration steps or values needed for whichever approach fits our setup, without executing any step that posts messages or creates the integration yet.
4. Draft an initial pinned message for the channel (e.g. incident protocol summary, link to runbooks) as a suggestion.
5. Prepare a list of initial members/roles to invite based on my answers.

Do not run the create command, do not install any integration, and do not invite members or post messages until I explicitly approve — this requires a human explicitly approves before changes are applied.

When done, report back: the exact channel name/visibility prepared, the integration approach identified with any values needed, the draft pinned message, and the proposed member list — clearly stop for human sign-off before applying any of it.

scale_009:n6.prompt:
You are helping me create a post-mortem template as part of our on-call & incidents setup. We use {{vendor}} (a project-management tool) for shared docs and project templates. If you don't already have it, ask me for: the {{vendor}} workspace/team name where this should live, and any existing folder or project it should sit under (e.g., an 'Incidents' or 'On-Call' space).

Goal: draft a reusable post-mortem template page in {{vendor}} that our team can duplicate for every incident. The template should include sections for: incident summary, timeline of events, root cause analysis, impact/severity, detection method, what went well, what went wrong, action items with owners and due dates, and links to related incident tickets or PagerDuty alerts.

Actions to take:
1. Draft the full template content (all sections above, with placeholder text/examples where helpful).
2. Using your configured credentials, create the new page in the specified {{vendor}} workspace via the API (create a new page, e.g., using an operation like POST /v1/pages) or the dashboard if that's easier, so it's saved as a duplicable template.
3. Confirm the page was created successfully and note its location/link.
4. Prepare a short checklist showing the template structure and where it now lives, ready for my review.

Because a human must explicitly approve before changes are applied, do NOT finalize, publish, share, or mark this template as the official standard yourself. Prepare the draft and the created page, then stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the draft template content, the link/location of the created {{vendor}} page, and a summary of what still needs my approval before it becomes the team's default post-mortem process.
